title: How the browser builds the page: DOM, CSSOM and rendering

videos.script: Nine lessons to get bytes from a server to a machine. Here is what happens to them afterwards, and it is more work than everything before it put together. {{arrived}} What arrived is text. Angle brackets, words, and references to other things it does not have yet. {{text}} What you see is a page: shapes with positions, colours, sizes, and text laid out in lines that were decided on the spot for this window at this width. {{page}} Nothing in the text said where anything goes. Not one coordinate. The browser worked out every one of them, in about a tenth of a second, and it will do it again if you turn the phone sideways. {{no-coordinates}} This lesson is the path between those two pictures, and it has a small number of steps. Read the markup into a tree. Read the styles into another one. Decide which parts are visible. Work out where they go, paint them, and put them on the screen. {{steps}} Learn those and two things follow. You can say why a page is blank while it is clearly loading. And you can say which of the things you did made it slower, which is the difference between guessing at performance and knowing. {{why}} The lesson after this one opens the tool that shows you all of it happening. {{title}}

One page, one timeline, and every step of this lesson on it. Here is the request going out. {{request}} The first bytes of HTML come back, and the parser starts immediately — it does not wait for the rest. {{first-bytes}} Twelve lines in, a stylesheet. The parser keeps reading the markup, and a second request goes out for the style. Nothing will be drawn until it comes back, because drawing without it would mean drawing the wrong thing and doing it twice. {{stylesheet}} Here is the gap. Watch the screen: it is blank, and the browser is working the whole time. That blankness is the thing people report as the site being slow, and it is this bar. {{gap}} A script, with no attributes. Parsing stops dead. The script is fetched, and then run, and only then does the markup carry on being read. Two things that had nothing to do with each other, in a queue, because of where a line sits in a file. {{script-block}} The style arrives. The tree of styles is built, joined to the tree of elements, and now there is something to lay out. {{combine}} Layout: every box, every position, every line of text, for this window at this width. Paint: the pixels. Composite: onto the screen. {{ltp}} And there it is. First paint. {{paint}} Now watch the last part, because it is the one that annoys people most. The font arrives late, and the text is redrawn. An image without dimensions finishes loading, and everything below it moves down. {{shift}} Neither of those was slow. Both of them are late, which is a different problem with different fixes, and both of them are in the reading. {{close}}
